title: Curated LLM: Synergy of LLMs and Data Curation for tabular augmentation in low-data regimes
summary: Argues that in the low-data regime a generator fitted to a handful of rows cannot invent structure it never saw, and proposes drawing candidate rows from a large language model's prior instead, then discarding the ones a learning-dynamics curation step marks as hard or ambiguous, so only samples the downstream model can actually use survive. CTGAN and TVAE are the conventional tabular generators the argument is set against and the comparison is run against: TVAE is the head-to-head generator in the extrapolation study and in the per-subgroup accuracy gains, where it loses ground on the smallest groups while the language model gains.
evidence: section 2.1 states that in the low-data regime conventional tabular generative models such as CTGAN and TVAE are constrained by the limited training set and may not generate sufficiently diverse or accurate synthetic data, which is the motivation for the language-model approach; the extrapolation study compares samples generated by GPT-4 against TVAE described as a widely used tabular data generator; the subgroup table reports average accuracy gains for GPT-4 against TVAE across the smallest subgroups

title: MargCTGAN: A "Marginally" Better CTGAN for the Low Sample Regime
summary: Observes that synthetic tabular data is usually judged only by downstream task usefulness and that this hides how models behave when the real sample is small, then evaluates several generators across fidelity, utility and marginal statistics in the low-sample regime, finding CTGAN strong on attribute fidelity but weak on utility while TableGAN is the reverse. MargCTGAN is the paper's answer to that split: it is built on CTGAN and adds feature matching of decorrelated marginals in the principal component space, keeping the rest of the model, and improves utility without giving up the fidelity CTGAN already had.
evidence: the abstract states that to capitalize on the strengths of both models the paper proposes MargCTGAN, which improves upon CTGAN by introducing feature matching of decorrelated marginals in the principal component space, and that this consistently improves utility; the same passage reports the popular CTGAN model demonstrating high attribute fidelity but falling short in utility for low-data scenarios; section 3 describes MargCTGAN as adhering to the standard GAN paradigm with generator and discriminator

title: ResBit: Residual Bit Vector for Categorical Values
summary: Replaces one-hot encoding of categorical values with residual bit vectors, a hierarchical binary representation whose length grows logarithmically rather than linearly in cardinality, so that tables with high-cardinality columns stay tractable for generative models that would otherwise blow up in input dimension. CTGAN and TVAE are the first two of six baselines, named as the de facto standards for tabular generation, and the analysis reports CTGAN winning F1 on one dataset, failing on a highly imbalanced one, and both models losing sample diversity.
evidence: the baselines paragraph states that six existing methods are used and that the first two are CTGAN and TVAE as the de facto standards, alongside TabDDPM, CoDi, StaSy and TabSyn; the introduction describes TVAE and CTGAN as the models applying VAE and GAN to tabular data generation and still used as baselines in the field; the results discussion reports CTGAN outperforming on F1 for the AR dataset, failing to generate effectively on the imbalanced CC dataset, and both CTGAN and TVAE showing a loss of diversity

title: TransCORALNet: A Two-Stream Transformer CORAL Networks for Supply Chain Credit Assessment Cold Start
summary: Attacks the cold-start problem in supply-chain credit assessment, where a new industry has no labelled default history, with a two-stream transformer whose shared-weight encoders take source-industry records in one stream and target-industry records in the other, aligned by a CORAL domain-adaptation loss and explained through LIME. CTGAN supplies the target stream: it is trained to model the target-domain feature distribution and the synthetic records it produces are what the lower stream consumes, so the cold-start result depends on it.
evidence: the contributions state that to facilitate the cold start problem the paper adopts a GAN-based method, CTGAN, to model tabular data distribution and generate synthetic data by learning the probability distribution of the features in the target domain; the architecture section states the lower stream's input is synthetic target training data generated by the CTGAN approach, with encoder blocks and fully connected layers sharing weights across the two streams; the framework figure includes the CTGAN procedures as a labelled component

title: Balanced Marginal and Joint Distributional Learning via Mixture Cramer-Wold Distance
summary: Notes that a generative model trained on a joint distributional distance can score well on joint metrics while fitting individual columns poorly, and proposes a mixture Cramer-Wold distance that adds marginal reconstruction to the joint objective, so a denoising autoencoder learns both at once with a tunable trade-off. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five synthesizers it is measured against on marginal and joint similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure, all trained at the same latent dimension with their hyperparameters recorded.
evidence: the experimental section states the model is compared with the state-of-the-art synthesizers CTGAN, TVAE, CTAB-GAN, CW2 and DistVAE, all at latent dimension two; Table 3 records the epochs, batch size and learning rate for CTGAN and TVAE; Table 6 ranks them on Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Wasserstein, pairwise correlation difference, log-cluster and F1, and Table 7 on distance to closest record and attribute disclosure
